methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)

data.narrative:
OBSIDIA Semiconductor is a seed-stage company in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The comparable universe consists of 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Two standard valuation methods are inapplicable here. Peer-Median triangulation fails due to insufficient narrow-stage peers: while 13 companies operate in the Chips & Semiconductors sector broadly, filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage competitors yields only 2 datapoints—below the threshold of 3 needed for statistical relevance. Using an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias. Public-Comp Anchoring, which could reference the sector's 20.4x median price-to-sales multiple across the three public comps, cannot be executed because OBSIDIA's revenue is not on file, a common limitation for private companies at seed stage.

Without disclosed revenue figures or a sufficiently dense peer set at equivalent stage and focus, this analysis cannot produce a quantified valuation range. The data supports only a negative conclusion: standard relative-value methods do not yield a defensible result. Progression to valuation would require either OBSIDIA's revenue disclosure or expansion of the private peer sample. Alternative approaches—such as bottom-up cost-of-capital models or venture-stage benchmarking by capital deployed—would require additional inputs not present in the current dataset.
